findings.title: Part D guard is placed on a function the success criterion's scenario never calls
findings.description:
The success criterion is "Re-running `sq review code <N>` over an edited review file archives the prior content and warns; nothing is silently destroyed." T12 adds the archive-on-overwrite guard exclusively to `save_review_file` (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:220`). But `sq review code <N>` does not use that function:

- `src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:746` calls `save_review_result(...)`.
- `save_review_result` writes directly via `path.write_text(...)` at `src/squadron/review/persistence.py:294` — it never calls `save_review_file`.
- `save_review_file` has exactly one production caller: `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:272`, and that call site is reached only in the `else` branch where `slice_info is None`. When `slice_info` is available (the ordinary `sq review code 305` case), the pipeline action also routes through `save_review_result` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:255`).

Net effect: after T12/T13, re-running `sq review code 305` over an edited review still silently overwrites the hand-written content. The data-loss hazard the slice names in its Value section ("re-running `sq review code <N>` destroys hand-written content in the review file with no warning") and in Verification Walkthrough step 7 is not closed. T13's tests only exercise `save_review_file` directly, so they would pass while the criterion stays false.

The guard belongs in `save_review_result` (the function both the CLI and the slice-info pipeline branch actually call), with `save_review_file` either delegated to it or guarded in parallel. The task's own wording "In `review/persistence.py`, before `save_review_file` writes to an existing `path`" is the place the implementation lands, but that is the wrong target for the criterion.

findings.title: Relocation leaves the review→pipeline import that the design's F002 rule exists to eliminate
findings.description:
The slice design states the rule the relocation exists to satisfy: "Having `review/resolution.py` import `pipeline/actions/` internals would invert that and create a review ↔ pipeline package-level cycle. So the context-free core *moves* into `review/addressed/` rather than being imported across the boundary." T1 moves `models.py` "verbatim — no logic changes," but that file carries `from squadron.pipeline.models import ActionResult` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/models.py:18`), used by `read_findings(result: ActionResult)`. After T1, `review/addressed/models.py` imports `squadron.pipeline.models` — a review→pipeline import, in the module the design labels "the context-free core."

T3 compounds this: it moves `verification.py` into `review/addressed/` while `verify_outcomes` has a runtime (non-`TYPE_CHECKING`) `from squadron.pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.screens import RoundDiff` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/verification.py:17`). T3 describes this as "a cross-package import in the pipeline→review direction," but the direction is the opposite: `review/addressed/verification.py` importing from `pipeline/...` is review→pipeline. T3's own wording is directionally wrong, and a junior AI following it literally would reproduce the inversion the design forbids.

Neither T1 nor T3 asks the implementer to make the relocated core genuinely context-free (e.g. move `RoundDiff` to `review/addressed/`, or drop the `ActionResult` type from the relocated reader). The design's own Cross-Slice Dependencies line "each importing the moved core in the already-established direction" is not satisfied by the tasks as written. This needs either a task to relocate `RoundDiff` and sever the `ActionResult` dependency, or an explicit design decision accepting the inversion — the current breakdown does neither, and T3 asserts the opposite of what the code will do.

findings.title: Success criterion 11 names two discovery surfaces; only one is tested
findings.description:
The criterion reads: "Metrology `discover_judge_results` **and review discovery** return no resolution artifacts (test against the real glob)." T32 tests only `discover_judge_results` (`src/squadron/metrology/discovery.py:27`, glob `*-review.*`). The second named surface — "review discovery" — is `metrology.capture.resolve_target` (`src/squadron/metrology/capture.py:97`, glob `{index}-review.*`), which resolves a review by bare slice index and raises an ambiguity error listing candidates. It is a separate function with its own glob, and it is not exercised by T32.

Both are safe by construction today (the resolution filename `{index}-resolution.{type}.{name}-r{n}.md` contains no `-review.` substring), but the criterion explicitly calls for the real glob on both, and the second is the one that a same-index review-plus-resolution pair would interact with. T32 should add a `resolve_target` case asserting that a directory containing both `305-review.code.x.md` and `305-resolution.code.x-r1.md` resolves unambiguously to the review and does not list the resolution artifact as a candidate.

findings.title: Part A does not cover the pipeline action's second persistence branch or the JSON output path
findings.description:
T10 states the pipeline path as "`pipeline/actions/review.py` (the pipeline-action path): same resolution and same fallback behavior." That action has **two** persistence branches (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:255` and `:272`): the first calls `save_review_result`, the second calls `format_review_markdown` and then `save_review_file` with pre-formatted content. Only the first can carry `reviewed_sha` through a new parameter; the second needs the stamp resolved into the `format_review_markdown` call before `save_review_file` receives the string. T10's wording does not distinguish them, so the second branch is a plausible omission.

Relatedly, `save_review_result` has a JSON branch (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:288`, reached by the CLI's `--json` flag on `review slice`/`arch`/`tasks`) that serializes `result.to_dict()` and never calls `format_review_markdown` — so it has no frontmatter to carry `reviewedSha`. The criterion says "carries `reviewedSha:` in frontmatter," which a JSON artifact does not have, but neither T10 nor T11 says what the JSON path should do. A junior AI could plausibly add the key to the JSON dict, omit it, or fail to notice the branch exists. T10 should state both explicitly: which branch receives the stamp and that the JSON writer is out of scope for the frontmatter criterion.

findings.title: T14's position after T12 inverts the design's stated sequence, mitigated by explicit gating language
findings.description: The design's Phase 5 note is unambiguous: "the cf `archive/`-scanning verification in Decision 7 must appear as its own checklist task in the breakdown, **sequenced before Part D lands**." T14 is numbered after T12/T13 and self-describes as "gates T12 in practice even though it is numbered after it." The mitigation is real — T12 carries an explicit "Do not mark this task done until T14's verification outcome is known" instruction and T14 repeats it — so this is not a functional gap. It is nonetheless an inversion of the design's stated sequence, and the simpler fix is to renumber T14 ahead of T12 so the checklist order matches the go/no-go the design asked for.

findings.title: T3's direction claim is contradicted by the code it describes
findings.description: T3 says `verification.py`'s `RoundDiff` import "stays as a cross-package import in the pipeline→review direction." The file moves to `review/addressed/` and `screens.py` stays in `pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/`, so the import runs review→pipeline. This is the same defect as the FAIL finding above, recorded separately here because the mislabeled direction is what would lead a junior AI to implement it without reconsidering the design rule. Correcting the label in T3 is a prerequisite to fixing the underlying placement.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage across both files is complete
findings.description:
All thirteen success criteria trace to at least one task, and the criteria deferred from file 1 to file 2 are explicitly declared in file 1's frontmatter (`projectState`), Context Summary, and Handoff section:

- Criterion 1 (`reviewedSha` from both paths) → T9, T10, T11 (with the branch-clarity caveat above).
- Criterion 2 (`resolve` produces artifact; review byte-identical) → T34, which asserts byte-identity directly rather than inferring it.
- Criterion 3 (empty diff → UNADDRESSED, zero judge calls) → T21, T22.
- Criterion 4 (`--no-judge` → UNKNOWN) → T25, T26.
- Criterion 5 (untouched-path claim → disputed) → T27, T28.
- Criterion 6 (legacy fallback + `--since` override) → T19, T20.
- Criterion 7 (re-review archives prior content) → T12, T13 — covered by task, but the target function is wrong (see FAIL finding above).
- Criterion 8 (FAIL/CONCERNS with zero CONCERN+ → UNKNOWN) → T23, T24, correctly isolated in its own task with its own test.
- Criterion 9 (judge failure / unreadable response / injection cap) → T25, T26.
- Criterion 10 (failed archive copy aborts) → T12, T13, with the fail-closed ERROR path and byte-identity assertion spelled out.
- Criterion 11 (discovery excludes resolutions) → T32 (second surface missing; see CONCERN above).
- Criterion 12 (305 suite unchanged after relocation) → T2, T4, T6, T8, with the "same count as before" check and the "no test needed rewriting" instruction in T6.
- Criterion 13 (second run writes `-r2`) → T31, T32, T34.

findings.title: Test-with discipline, commit markers, and task sizing are sound
findings.description: Every implementation task in file 1 is immediately followed by its test task (T1→T2, T3→T4, T5→T6, T7→T8, T9+T10→T11, T12→T13; T14 is a verification checkpoint, not an implementation task). File 2 continues the pattern without exception (T15→T16 … T39, T40 is closeout). Commit markers are plain lines on working, tested points — six in file 1 at T2, T4, T6, T8, T11, T13 and a dense but justified series in file 2 — not after every task and not only at the end. Task sizes are appropriate for a junior AI: the largest (T25, effort 3/5) names four distinct behaviors and one explicit "flag to the Project Manager, do not silently add scope" boundary; T5 similarly gives an exact function signature, a precise body boundary, and the two symbols that must stay behind. The two-file split is proportional to the slice's three-part dependency structure (Part 0 infrastructure → Parts B–C consumers), and file 1's Context Summary explains why file 2 cannot start early.

Relocation leaves the review→pipeline import that the design's F002 rule exists to eliminate
Success criterion 11 names two discovery surfaces; only one is tested
Part A does not cover the pipeline action's second persistence branch or the JSON output path
T14's position after T12 inverts the design's stated sequence, mitigated by explicit gating language
T3's direction claim is contradicted by the code it describes
